audience.notes: Australian couples in their 30s planning a luxury wedding, budget AUD 150K+. They have seen the survey averages and know they do not apply. Paying parents want to see where money goes and what hidden costs to expect. Do not write tips for weddings under $10,000 or 'how to save' listicles.

payload.search_intent: Informational. Searchers want a number; we give them an honest explanation of why no reliable one exists, then the tools to build their own figure.
payload.angle: USER DECISION: no headline average dollar figure at all. The piece states, with official sources, that no current government average exists (ABS records marriages, not their cost; Moneysmart gives budgeting guidance), explains why the survey averages that dominate the SERP mislead, compares costs by category and how they scale at the luxury end, lists the costs couples forget, and shows how a destination wedding compares. A Wedded Advisor is shown handling the invisible work.
serp_gaps_to_win: Only page saying plainly, with ABS and Moneysmart links, that there is no current official average
Explains mean vs median, self-selected samples and inclusions behind survey averages
Luxury-tier category guidance (AUD 150K+), absent from the top 10
Home vs destination comparison for Australians, linking our cost guides
Forgotten costs and contract protections with ACCC guidance

outline.h2: Why There Is No Official Average Wedding Cost in Australia
outline.answers: Is there a real, current number?
must_include: ABS Marriages and Divorces, Australia records how many couples marry, not what they spend (link abs.gov.au; researcher to confirm and check whether any ABS series covers wedding spending)

Moneysmart offers wedding budgeting guidance; researcher to confirm whether any average appears on the current page and its date. If an old figure appears, say it is dated without quoting it as a current average
Figures quoted online come from industry surveys run by businesses that sell to couples; say so without naming blocked sources or repeating their numbers
Answer the keyword in the first 100 words

outline.answers: Why should I not plan around a survey average?
must_include: Mean vs median in plain words: a few large weddings pull the mean up
Self-selected online samples, differing inclusions (rings, honeymoon, attire), and different guest counts
Our own older surveys found the mean well above the median; describe the pattern only, no figures
Why an 'average' says nothing about a 150-guest luxury wedding

outline.answers: Which decisions move the total most?
must_include: Guest count as the main multiplier (per-head catering, beverages, seating, favours)
City and venue type (harbourside, winery, private estate, hotel ballroom)
Date, season and day of week
Level of service and inclusions in venue packages

faqs.q: What is the average wedding cost in Australia?
faqs.a_brief: Honest answer without a figure: there is no current official average; ABS counts marriages, not spending; published averages come from industry surveys and vary widely; your cost depends on guest count, city, date and inclusions.

faqs.q: Why do websites quote different average wedding costs?
faqs.a_brief: Different surveys, samples, years, inclusions and mean vs median.

faqs.q: What is the biggest wedding expense in Australia?
faqs.a_brief: Venue and catering, priced per head, so guest count drives it.

faqs.q: Is a destination wedding cheaper than a wedding in Australia?
faqs.a_brief: It can be for a smaller guest list, but compare like with like; link the destination vs home cost guide.

faqs.q: How much contingency should we keep in a wedding budget?
faqs.a_brief: Follow Moneysmart budgeting guidance (researcher to confirm wording); keep a separate line for surcharges, overtime and weather.
